policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Official NIST ITL AI Program standards page (originally published 2021-08-03 and updated through March 6, 2026). Describes NIST's non-regulatory standards strategy: the AI Standards Zero Drafts pilot, A Plan for Global Engagement on AI Standards (NIST AI 100-5e2025, July 26, 2024), federal interagency coordination via ICSP/AISCWG, alignment of AI RMF 1.0 with international ISO/IEC standards and crosswalks, and GCR-26-069 (Jan 15, 2026) on evaluating AI standards development.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The page is overwhelmingly framed around innovation_enablement, arguing that stakeholder-driven voluntary consensus standards, zero-draft pilots, and international RMF alignment accelerate standards creation, unleash AI innovation, and foster trustworthy AI adoption ecosystems. Innovation_enablement clearly edges out economic_competitiveness, which appears as a secondary rationale via alignment with the National Standards Strategy for Critical and Emerging Technology and U.S. Leadership in AI plan. Social_stability (public trust) and consumer_public_safety (managing AI risks for trustworthy development and use) play supporting roles.
